description: Hosts a 64-bit VST 2 or VST 3 instrument inside Rack: pitch and gate become MIDI notes, 16 of the plugin's parameters take CV, and its audio comes back out

inputs.text: 0V to 10V over the VST parameter mapped to it. Click its label and move a knob or slider in the plugin's editor to map one, or right-click the label to pick from a list
1V/oct pitch, rounded to the nearest note as the gate rises. A polyphonic cable here plays the plugin polyphonically
A rise here starts a MIDI note at the pitch on the CV input, and the note is held until this falls to 0V

outputs.text: Left channel of the audio the plugin produces
Right channel of the audio the plugin produces

notes: the module does nothing until a VST plugin is loaded into it. Click the plugin name, which reads No plugin until then, and pick from the VST plugins found on your system
the editor window of the plugin opens when it loads, and the eye beside the plugin name reopens it after you close it
the menu opened by clicking the plugin name, not the panel menu, is where VST search directories are added and removed. The search is recursive and runs at once, with no Rack restart
a parameter label reads as three dashes until it is mapped. Click it and move a control in the plugin's editor to map that one; right-click it for a list to pick from instead
a parameter label's right-click menu offers MIDI events as well as the plugin's own parameters: velocity, pitch wheel, mod wheel, sustain pedal, key pressure, note gates and transport
the factory presets map all 16 parameter inputs to MIDI note gates an octave apart, which turns the module into 16 drum pads for a drum machine plugin
many VST plugins are not built for fast parameter changes, so audio-rate modulation into a parameter input can crash the plugin or run heavy on CPU
menu: Block size — how many samples are gathered before the plugin is asked to process them, each choice printed with its latency: 128 by default, 16 at the least, 4096 at the most
Use worker thread — processes the plugin on a thread of its own; switch it off and the plugin is processed on Rack's engine thread
MIDI panic — releases every MIDI note the module is holding in the hosted plugin
